extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom leaders, media scholars, and journalism school students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for investigating reporter fraud, evaluating newsroom practices, and reforming standards and training at major newspapers. Covers how to run internal inquiries, publish corrections, and implement safeguards to prevent fabrication and plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold truth and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The cardinal tenet of journalism is simply truth; reporters must not fabricate, concoct scenes, lift material from others, or mislead readers and colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report states: 'Every newspaper ... trusts its employees to uphold central principles, and the inquiry found that Mr. Blair repeatedly violated the cardinal tenet of journalism, which is simply truth.' Violations include fabricated comments, concocted scenes, and plagiarism; upholding truth is the foundational evaluation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accounting and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations should provide a public accounting of serious errors and misconduct rather than handling them only privately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper contrasts past quiet/internal handling with the Times' public, lengthy report and corrections. Examples: publishing editor's notes, multi-page investigative pieces documenting errors, and public corrections lists to 'correct the record.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent investigative review team
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a specialized team (reporters, editors, investigators, legal staff) to examine alleged misconduct with sufficient independence from daily newsroom operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Times formed a team of reporters, editors and researchers (including legal correspondents) and moved them to a separate workspace; the composition should include investigative expertise and, where useful, legal rigor and diversity to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and composition of review team
rubrics_metrics.description: Select team members for specific skills and perspective (investigative reporters, legal background, media beat experience, demographic/experiential diversity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection reasoning in the report: Liptak and Glater were chosen for legal rigor; Barstow for investigative experience; Steinberg for media-reporting experience; adding a reporter who was young and black filled representational concerns. Team makeup should address both competence and newsroom representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational and physical separation for inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Physically isolate the investigation team from the newsroom and remove their normal access to newsroom systems to protect the integrity and independence of the inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team was moved to the 11th floor and had computers removed from their desks; 'we could not do this and work in the newsroom'—isolation reduces influence and preserves source confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to comprehensive documents and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Request and examine all relevant materials: all articles, work at prior outlets, internal communications about the reporter, application/resume, employee evaluations, personnel file, reimbursement requests, memos tracking corrections, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team drew up a list including 'all of Blair’s articles from the Times, examples of Blair’s work at The Boston Globe and The Washington Post, ... internal communications about Blair or his work at the paper, his application and resume, all his employee evaluations, his personnel file, his reimbursement requests, and any internal memos tracking corrections or error rates.' Full access is essential to reconstruct patterns of behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define scope and depth of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Set a clear, manageable scope for the inquiry (timeframe, beats, or all work) balancing thoroughness and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team decided to focus first on national-staff work (about six months) as the most manageable starting point rather than attempting an initial exhaustive review of all four years of work; scope should be justified and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough, itemized corrections and error reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile and publish a comprehensive list of corrections for affected stories, not just narrative descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Times published two pages containing the narrative and two pages listing corrections for Blair’s stories; the report underscores the need for explicit correction lists to 'correct the record.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold editors and managers accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and report on the roles of supervisors, assignment editors, and management practices that allowed misconduct to persist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inquiry 'would need to report on their superiors' and asked difficult questions about editorial oversight and failures of communication among senior editors, implying that accountability extends beyond the individual reporter to systemic editorial choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on one’s own organization requires special protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Create procedures for newsroom self-reporting that ensure independence from usual chains of command and protect investigative integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal protocol ('editors talk to editors') was set aside; Boyd warned that some records might not be shared—indicating a need for pre-established protocols to manage conflicts when investigating colleagues and superiors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize correcting the record over institutional point-scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus the inquiry’s work on establishing facts and documenting errors rather than allowing the investigation to be used primarily as a vehicle for internal political battles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters resisted turning the Blair inquiry into a takedown of Howell Raines; their assignment was to 'explain Jayson Blair' and 'root out Blair’s errors and correct the record,' emphasizing corrective aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in senior-level standards and training positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Create masthead-level positions (e.g., public editor/ombudsman, standards editor, career development editor) to codify practices and oversee standards and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Blair, the Times created a public editor, a standards editor, and a career development editor; these roles were presented as concrete institutional reforms to shore up standards and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory training and performance evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Require newsroom leaders to take management/ethics training and implement mandatory annual reviews for all staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Times instituted two-day management training covering 'ethics, standards and accuracy' and made annual reviews mandatory; a database of every job was created to support career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onboarding, mentoring and formal orientation for new hires
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce structured orientation and mentoring systems so new employees are formally introduced to standards, peers, and the newsroom culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New hires now get 'mandatory sessions to teach new employees about the Times standards and practices ... and a prescribed mentoring system'—a move away from informal, ad hoc assimilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement fact-checking safeguards (spot checks and audits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute spot checks—either pre-publication when feasible or post-publication—on randomly selected stories to deter and detect fabrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper discusses proposals such as random spot checks (noting practical limits at daily papers), and cites the Fort Worth Star-Telegram as performing pre-publication checks on local stories; the aim is deterrence and detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use random post-publication surveys to sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Send random post-publication surveys to sources quoted in stories to verify reporting and gather source feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steve Brill's practice of sending surveys to sources (as at Brill’s Content) is cited as a means both to catch fabrication and to let reporters know subjects' reactions; Brill argued such surveys helped catch a fabricating reporter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize responding to red flags and suspicion
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aggressive and prompt in investigating signs of suspicion (internal complaints, anomalous patterns) even when full-scale fact-checking is impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sulzberger's response favored aggressive response to signs of suspicion and use of the public editor rather than attempting full-time pre-publication fact-checking across all beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial standards: sourcing, attribution, and avoiding passive constructions as substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforce rigor in sourcing, attribution and active sourcing practices; avoid passive voice, speculation, mind-reading, and overstatement without evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baron’s internal critique of Lewinsky coverage called out 'repeating sensational reports…without confirming them,' 'passive voice…as a substitute for sourcing,' 'speculation,' and 'overstatement'—these are explicit substantive standards for evaluating journalism quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify logistical claims (travel, presence, expenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corroborate reporters' claims of travel and field presence by checking expenses, reimbursements, travel receipts, and other logistical records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An initial hypothesis in the inquiry concerned whether Blair had exhausted company credit and whether travel records matched dispatches; the team sought reimbursement requests and receipts as part of verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource-aware implementation: tailor safeguards to operational realities
rubrics_metrics.description: Design checks and standards that account for daily deadlines and resource constraints; use targeted pre- or post-publication processes where full fact-checking is infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report acknowledges that 'a traditional fact checking process would obviously be impossible at a daily newspaper' and discusses feasible alternatives (random checks, surveys, aggressive responses to red flags).
